anomalies.observed: On the EthernetAndPower sheet the DC barrel jack J7 (Barrel_Jack_Switch) carries the note '2 and 3 are shorted with no plug / 1 is center, center is positive'. Tracing the wires, the pin labelled 1 (the center/positive contact) is tied to GND, the pin tied to the BAT+/VIN/VBUS node is 2, and the remaining switch pin is tied to NET0048 (the raw battery-positive node at the anode of U5 / U1+). Thus the center positive pin is shorted to ground and the sleeve/switch contacts do not implement the intended GND / BAT- roles.
anomalies.expected: Per the specification the jack must be wired J4.1→BAT+ (center/positive), J4.2→GND (sleeve), J4.3→BAT-, so that the normally-shorted 2-3 pair keeps the battery return connected to GND and a DC plug both powers BAT+ through the center pin and disconnects the battery. The center pin must never be on GND.

evidence.quote: Netlist: J4.1→BAT+ (center/positive), J4.2→GND (sleeve), J4.3→BAT-. Since pins 2 and 3 are normally shorted (per the note)... the jack's internal switch keeps the battery's return path connected to GND by default, and inserting a DC plug breaks that short — disconnecting the battery.

anomalies.impact: With a DC adapter plugged in, the adapter's positive center pin is shorted to ground (and the sleeve is held at BAT+), causing a hard short / reversed polarity on the power input; the battery-disconnect logic is also broken. This matches the 'DC plug pins are wrong, shorts battery' failure that the intended rev-D design was supposed to fix.
